name: Huang Guanxiong
current_role: Chairman and actual controller, Guangdong DYMATIC Chemicals Group (SZSE: 002054), Shunde, Foshan
profile: Huang Guanxiong (b. 1965) founded DYMATIC's predecessor Demei Industrial in 1998 and built it into a listed maker of textile printing/dyeing auxiliaries and fine chemicals. He directly holds ~19.4% (≈21% with his holding company). He stepped down as general manager in 2023 but remains chairman and signed the 2024 annual report.
interesting_fact: He controls about 21% of DYMATIC directly and via Foshan Shunde Demei Chemical Group, and remains its chairman after handing the GM role to Chen Qiuyou in March 2023.
deep_cut_fact: After finishing high school in 1981 he worked at the Shunde agricultural machinery factory; in 1983 he started his own business in transport and chemical-materials trading before co-founding Shunde Jinghua in 1996 and Demei in 1998.
notes: Low public profile; the IR email belongs to board secretary Zhu Minchong (company securities office), per the 2024 annual report. Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Soshil Kumar Jain
profile: Founder and chairman of Panacea Biotec (founded 1984 as Panacea Drugs). Died 7 October 2022 at age 89.
notes: Deceased 7 Oct 2022 (sources: https://medicaldialogues.in/news/industry/pharma/panacea-biotec-chairman-soshil-kumar-passes-away-at-age-of-89-100381 ; https://biospectrumindia.com/news/66/22078/founder-chairman-of-panacea-biotec-passes-away.html). Company now led by his son Rajesh Jain as Chairman & MD.

profile: Shantaben P. Jain is a member of the Jain promoter family of Kewal Kiran Clothing, the Mumbai apparel maker behind the Killer, Lawman Pg3 and Integriti brands run by the Pukhraj Jain brothers (CMD Kewalchand P. name: Chinh Chu
current_role: Founder and Senior Managing Director, CC Capital (New York private equity); director of Getty Images and other portfolio companies
profile: Vietnamese-born American dealmaker who spent ~25 years at Blackstone (joined 1990), rising to senior managing director and co-chair of private equity. He left in 2015 to found CC Capital, which led deals including Dun & Bradstreet's take-private, Utz Brands' SPAC listing, E2open and Getty Images' listing.
interesting_fact: Chu summited Mount Everest on 17 May 2023, guided by record-holding Sherpa Kami Rita.
deep_cut_fact: To pay for college at the University at Buffalo he sold educational books door-to-door for Southwestern Co., building a sales team and becoming a top seller; he also worked as a telemarketer raising funds for UB. After a 1999 flood he co-founded Vietnam Relief Effort with his sister.
notes: Fled Saigon at age 8 in 1975 on one of the last US military refugee flights. Best route is CC Capital's published media contacts (Karv / Joele Frank).

name: Prakash Harakchand Parakh
current_role: Managing Director, Parakh Agro Industries Ltd (Parakh Group, Pune); heads group real estate arm Gemini Housing
profile: Second-generation leader of Pune's Parakh Group, a Maharashtra trading house that moved into wheat flour, pulses and edible oil in the 1980s. He drove the edible-oil business, sold to Cargill in 2005, then refocused on atta/pulses, flexible packaging (Parakh Flexipacks), wind power and real estate; the group re-entered oil refining in 2017.
interesting_fact: Parakh pioneered flexible pouches for edible oil in India and claims the first 10 kg atta pack; Fortune India named it the fastest-growing mid-size FMCG company in 2017-18.
deep_cut_fact: Per the group's own site, he set up what it calls Asia's largest edible-oil refinery under one roof at Kurkumbh in 1999, and was appointed a non-executive director of Bank of Maharashtra on the recommendation of Maharashtra's Chief Minister.
notes: Privately held family group; MD listing per MCA-based directories (DIN 00337188). Brother Suresh Parakh and third-generation Harshal Parakh also active. Web search budget ran out mid-research; Cargill deal details from packaging trade press only.

name: Jane Nind Fraser
current_role: Chair (since Oct 2025) and CEO (since 2021), Citigroup Inc.
profile: Scottish-born banker (b. 1967, St Andrews) who became the first woman to run a major US bank when she took over as Citigroup CEO in 2021, adding the chair role in October 2025. A former McKinsey partner, she joined Citi in 2004 and ran Citi Private Bank, CitiMortgage, US consumer banking and Latin America; she is leading Citi's multi-year simplification and restructuring.
interesting_fact: Fortune ranked her No. 1 on its 2026 Most Powerful Women list; she was made a Dame (DBE).
deep_cut_fact: Before banking leadership, she co-authored the 1999 book 'Race for the World: Strategies to Build a Great Global Firm' with three McKinsey colleagues, and early on worked as a brokerage associate at Asesores Bursátiles in Madrid (1990-92).
notes: Very high-profile CEO; requests go through Citi Corporate Communications (US media hotline 212-793-0710 published on the same page). Educated at Girton College, Cambridge and Harvard Business School.

name: Andrew John Morton
current_role: Head of Markets and member of the Executive Management Team, Citigroup
profile: Andy Morton runs Citi's global Markets business. He joined Citi in 2008 after ~15 years at Lehman Brothers, where he rose to Global Head of Fixed Income, and at Citi previously led G10 Rates and Financing and the markets quantitative analysis function.
interesting_fact: He began his career as an academic in mathematical finance, with a maths degree from Waterloo and a PhD from Cornell.
deep_cut_fact: He is the 'M' in the Heath-Jarrow-Morton (HJM) framework, the interest-rate model he co-authored that is still widely used to value interest-rate derivatives.
notes: Low media profile; a quant-finance angle (HJM) is a natural hook. Route via Citi Markets comms.

name: Mark W Begor
current_role: CEO and director, Equifax Inc. (since April 2018); director, Raymond James Financial
profile: A 35-year GE veteran who ran GE Energy Management, GE Capital Real Estate and GE Capital Retail Finance (now Synchrony) and was CFO of NBCUniversal, then a Warburg Pincus managing director. He took over Equifax after its 2017 breach, led a ~$3bn cloud rebuild and grew revenue from $3.4bn (2018) to about $6.1bn (2025).
interesting_fact: Equifax has completed 15 acquisitions totalling nearly $4bn since 2021 under his leadership.
deep_cut_fact: Outside Equifax he chairs the board of trustees of Dartmouth Health and is a trustee of the U.S. Ski and Snowboard Foundation; earlier he led GE's investor-relations function.
notes: Syracuse University BA, RPI MBA. Left the NCR Atleos board in May 2025 per Equifax bio. Route via Equifax media relations.

name: Jason Wilk
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Dave Inc. (Nasdaq: DAVE)
profile: Los Angeles entrepreneur who sold video ad network AllScreen (Y Combinator, Mark Cuban-backed) for a reported $85m in 2015, then founded Dave in 2016 as an overdraft-fee-free banking app. Dave grew past 10 million members, went public via SPAC in January 2022, and he still runs it as CEO.
interesting_fact: He says he took more than 120 VC meetings to fund Dave, which was inspired by his own frustration with overdraft fees; he testified to a Senate Banking subcommittee in 2022.
deep_cut_fact: A Loyola Marymount golfer who once aimed to turn pro, his first venture was golf-equipment site 1DaySports.com, which he sold for $100,000 and used to fund a multi-continent backpacking trip; he also co-founded WriteyBoard, selling stick-on whiteboards to startups.
notes: Founder-CEO with an open, story-driven public persona (fintech/overdraft disruption) - good podcast fit. Media contact Dan Ury per Nov 2026 earnings release.
